To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) antipyrine transfer differed significantly between laboratories and therefore normalization of the data was necessary; 2) antipyring normalization generated a good ranking of the compounds; 3) compounds that are similar to antiprine in their transplacenta transport and recovery were ranked high in all studies and laboratories; and 4) antipyrin normalization resulted in the ranking order: NDMA ≥EtOH ≥ BPA≥ IQ ≥AA ≥GA ≥PCB180

antipyrine transfer rate in the ex vivo placental transfer model is a reliable and reproducible parameter to normalize data and to make them directly and unambiguously comparable and rankable, and that the normalized antipyrine AUC(120) is a useful parameter to rank compounds according to their placental transfer rate.
the placental transfer of the studied genotoxic and immunotoxins was in the order NDMA, EtOH, BPA, IQ, AA, GA, PCB180, PhIP, AFB1, DON, BP, PCB52, and TCDD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a standardized method for the assessment of the transfer rate of xenobiotics across the human placenta in vitro.
the placental transfer of genotoxic and immunotoxins.
the development of a methodological approach to compare and rank compounds with regard to their transplacentally transferable fraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antipyrine can be used as a normalizer for the placental perfusion technique, but that it is important to use a common normalization factor for all studies in order to compare the results between studies.
the compounds are ranked as follows: EtOH ≥ NDMA ≥ BPA ≥ AFB1 ≥ IQ ≥ AA ≥ GA ≥ PCB52 ≥ PhIP > BP ≥ DON ≥ PCB180 ≥ TCDD.
the antipyrine correction method is a good way to normalize placental transfer of the tested compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

antipyrine is an excellent marker to normalize data in ex vivo placenta perfusion studies, as it is a compound with a high transfer rate, good recovery in the media and low accumulation in the tissue.
antipyrine can be used as an internal control for placental perfusion experiments.
the placental transfer rate is a compound-specific characteristic that is not dependent on the laboratory or study design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the placenta is a very effective barrier for the majority of the compounds studied.

antipyrine is a useful reference compound in ex vivo human placental perfusion experiments and that it is possible to normalize placental perfusion parameters to correct for differences in experimental conditions.
the ranking of compounds according to transplacental passage is not influenced by the method of analysis, but is mainly determined by the physico-chemical properties of the compound.
